notes: The booklet has no inventory page with Element IDs, so every element ID was matched by eye to the closest catalogue entry. Colours are in props.
The main body is a dark-grey wedge plate. The nearest catalogue entry, lego-wedge-plate-4x4-cut, is a guess.

The body is drawn with a blue plate already on it in step 1, and a light-grey piece appears between the two blue plates in step 2. I modelled two blue 2x2 plates plus a light-grey 2x2 plate, all on body studs.

The black arm in cockpit step 2 does not appear in any parts box. To keep clip joins valid I modelled it as a plain rod (lego-6093525) clipped between the cockpit plate (lego-4219913) and the body's underside clip plate (lego-clip-plate-1x2, step 6). The real piece has a curled end.

Catalogue entries with a single stud port cannot name a separate port per attached part (the body wedge plate, the round plate under the sub-assembly, the plate with side pins, and the pod blue plates). Where a port holds several parts I named it on one edge and left it null on the others, which means a stud connection with no specific port.

The sub-assembly in step 5 is a round plate 2x2, a blue 1x2 plate, a light-grey 1x2 plate with side pins and two trans-light-blue round plates. Its two pins hold the clips of the two side pods in step 7.

The side pod is built 2x (copy 2 clips onto pin.2). Per pod I modelled two blue 1x4 plates, two curved slopes and two grille tiles. Step 4 may show an extra blue plate per pod, which I could not confirm.
The black clip plate under the body (step 3) is modelled as joined to the body, but it may press onto the blue plate.
